subject: Re: FirstBank RFP - traffic anchoring, gating and fallback playbook
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@firstbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@firstbank.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T16:12:00Z
Subject: RFP Annex A - requested detailed activation/rollback playbook

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the quick submission so far. As part of the RFP we need a focused section that outlines your staged activation (traffic anchoring), gating criteria, rollback triggers and timeline for integration with our environment. Specifically, procurement would like:

- A step-by-step activation sequence (including preflight checks, canary progression percentages and duration per step)
- Observable gating metrics (latency, error-rate, quality regressions) and concrete thresholds that would block progression
- Automated and manual rollback procedures, including required approvals and time-to-failure SLAs
- Expected maintenance windows and any planned brief downtimes for final cutover
- A minimal test-plan for smoke, soak and load phases that we can run with our SREs

Can you provide a standalone playbook we can include in Annex A by Friday (2026-07-24)? I attached the RFP AnnexA that outlines the fields we must fill. Also include any SOC2/audit evidence pointers.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Lead, Cloud Procurement
FirstBank

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-07-20T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP Annex A - requested detailed activation/rollback playbook

Hi Samantha — thanks, we can do that. I attached a first-draft playbook (RBW-activation-playbook-v1.pdf) that addresses the sequence and high-level gates; below is a short summary and a couple of clarifying questions so we align to your constraints.

Summary (playbook v1):
- Preflight (Day -7 to Day -1): config validation, schema checks, contract tests, secrets/cert verification
- Smoke canary (Day 0): 1% traffic for 12 hours; verify p50/p95 latency and error rate (<1% errors)
- Incremental ramp (Day 1-3): 10% for 24h -> 25% for 24h -> 50% for 24h (monitoring and quality validation at each step)
- Full cutover (Day 4): shift remaining traffic during low-usage window; final validation and decommission toggle for legacy endpoint
- Rollback: automated traffic diversion to previous model version if p99 latency increase >40% or sustained error rate >2% for 15min; manual rollback if quality regression flagged by evaluation set or prod-issue ticket triaged by SRE/CS.

Clarifying questions:
1) What is your allowable maintenance window (UTC) for final cutover?
2) Do you require an explicit approval step from procurement or security for each ramp step, or only for full cutover?
3) Any data residency constraints for the canary traffic (e.g., routing only to specific AZs)?

I looped in Grace (Solutions Engineering) and Aditya (Customer Success) who will help produce the final version and test-plan.

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RBW-activation-playbook-v1.pdf (draft)

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@firstbank.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@firstbank.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T14:50:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP Annex A - requested detailed activation/rollback playbook

Michael — thanks for the draft. A few clarifications from our side:

- Performance targets: our procurement and SRE teams require p99 inference <= 30s under peak expected load for the canary and ramp phases; please call out how Redwood plans to maintain that SLA during ramp.
- Maintenance window: final cutover must occur only within Sunday 02:00–04:00 UTC or approved emergency windows.
- Approvals: we require an auto-advance for canary -> ramp (no procurement approval) provided gating metrics pass; procurement/security sign-off only required for full cutover.
- Data residency: canaries must originate from us-east-1 only for the first 72 hours.
- Audit evidence: include SOC2 attestation references and point us to where the audit report can be requested.

Looping in our procurement doc (attached) for SOC2 checklist and the procurement mailbox to ensure they track dates.

Samantha Ortiz
Lead, Cloud Procurement
FirstBank

Attachment: FirstBank-RFP-SOC2-Checklist.xlsx (reference)

Subject: Updated playbook (v2) — gating thresholds, residency, rollback automation

Samantha / Procurement team — attached is RBW-activation-playbook-v2.pdf. Key changes addressing your notes:

- Performance & gating: p99 target called out with alerting hooks. Canary auto-abort if p99 > 30s for 10m or error rate >1% for 5m. During ramp, abort if p99 degrades >25% vs baseline or error rate >1.5% sustained 10m.
- Canary residency: first 72h anchored to us-east-1 only; traffic routing and IP allowlist included.
- Approvals: canary -> ramp auto-advance on gate pass; full cutover requires designated procurement and security emails to acknowledge via Doc (DocuSign link in playbook).
- Rollback automation: service mesh rule packaged to flip traffic to previous model version automatically on triggers; manual rollback runbook includes required Slack/Email approvals and expected time-to-restore (<=15 minutes for traffic diversion of 100%).
- Tests: smoke (5 synthetic requests), soak (24h load at 10% traffic), load (simulated peak traffic for 2h). Test checklist and required artifacts specified.

We also included a minimal telemetry checklist for SRE: custom traces, token-level cost counters, model-output sampling for evaluation, and a short list of dashboards we will hand over.

Next steps:
- Grace to schedule a 60-minute walkthrough with your SREs and App teams next week (available slots Tue/Wed).
- Aditya to provide estimated professional services days for the final integration and smoke tests.

Let us know if adjustments are required; we can produce a redlined version for Annex A.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
